text: Refines D-0345 and D-0351 for #648, step 8 of #571's statechart plan: a revision or amendment shows its checked reader chart beside a comparison with its baseline. A new project's revision compares with the preceding selected proposal whose checked reader validates, so a failed draft is never a baseline. An amendment compares with the ratified project captured at one resolved commit, keeping it through revisions, answers and recovery until another ratification of the project lands or the issue names another project; the revision then amends the project as it is now. Answers carry the baseline without becoming revisions, and refused, oversized and unsupported drafts keep the previous proposal for the next revision. A comparison binds exact model, include, view and lock identities and both bounds, and qualifies view changes, model-source changes and differing scopes. TLC picks its fingerprint polynomial afresh on every run, so concrete members are evidence, never identities: a common state changes only with its counts, rules or unavailable actions, and an arrow with its count, occurrence actions or hiding rules. Reports name each change once by reader label and counts. A legacy source without a view needs a drafting-supplied baseline/view.json, checked at its original bounds. Missing or stale required comparisons refuse publication. Ratification writes .invariant/comparison.json outside the lock and statement hash; synthesis carries the original's; verification validates it beside the independently computed final chart, and damaged or undrawable evidence becomes a printable diagnostic. None of it changes verdicts, assurance, fingerprints or locks, and equal charts claim no behavioral equivalence. Before merging, the merger fixed 15 defects the review confirmed, each with a test, and ran the pinned-TLC comparison coverage.
